excerpts.why: The September 2026 statement reports a rate raise, which cuts against the thesis of a 25 basis point cut at the October meeting.
It confirms the next FOMC meeting date of October 27–28, 2026, which is needed to judge the event timing.
This 2025 minutes excerpt describes historical yield-curve moves and serves only as background on how Treasury yields behaved around policy meetings.
It attributes rising longer-term yields to higher term premiums rather than policy easing, which weakens the link from a rate cut to lower long-bond yields that TLT depends on.
It describes market uncertainty from geopolitics and Treasury buyback implementation, which is background that could move long-duration Treasuries in either direction.
Stable longer-term inflation expectations give the Fed room to ease, which modestly supports a 25 basis point cut.
It warns that persistent inflation above target could unanchor expectations, which argues against the Fed cutting rates.
The September projections show a large majority of participants expecting rate increases, which directly undercuts the expectation of a cut in October.
